_readme: Curated player notes extracted from podcast/press briefings pasted into the assistant. Hand-reviewed and version-controlled: no live model runs at build time. Notes are DISPLAY-ONLY - they never feed the simulator. Every note keeps its source and, where possible, a verbatim quote, so a reader can judge it. Names that a transcript garbled are parked in `unresolved` rather than guessed at, because attaching a note to the wrong player is worse than dropping it.

players.quote: Harry Maguire marking one of his own players and marking him so well that he fouled him.

players.name: Vuskovic
players.note: 19-year-old Croatian international; standout in defence, contrasting with struggling high-priced signings elsewhere (surname-only in the briefing).

players.name: Anthony Elanga
players.note: A counter-attacking threat against Liverpool's very high line in the 2-2 draw.
players.quote: They are like the 'Slow Horses' of football... MI5 misfits... but they were full of running.

players.name: Lewis Miley
players.note: At 20, part of a young Newcastle midfield pivot; the performance was seen as a marked improvement on last season.

players.name: Ibrahim Sangare
players.note: Seamless debut in midfield, cited as evidence of Brentford's succession planning (surname-only in the briefing).

players.name: Enzo Fernandez
players.note: Named among high-value signings the briefing says need patient integration; early results are favouring settled squads.

players.name: Cole Palmer
players.note: Silky and fluid in the 3-2 win at Fulham, scoring a cheeky goal; his omission from the World Cup squad is read as a wake-up call after an injury-hit campaign.
players.quote: He just looked free, fluid, so silky, so clever on the ball... the goal was brilliant. He kind of gives Leno the eyes, makes it look like he's going to pass it back into the middle and then just rolls it through his legs. It's so cheeky. It's so Cole Palmer.

players.name: Robert Sanchez
players.note: Poorly positioned for both Fulham goals; the panic he transmits unsettles the defence. Seen as the single thing keeping Chelsea to top-four rather than title contention.
players.quote: It's not just the first goal with Josh King. It's also things like just the the panic that he transmits... It just makes the defense nervy, I think. This is Sanchez's fourth season as Chelsea's number one, and it just feels like he's been an issue for all of that period.

players.name: Joao Pedro
players.note: Part of a Chelsea front three with Palmer and Rogers described as one of the most exciting attacking units in the league.

players.name: Morgan Rogers
players.note: Part of a Chelsea front three with Palmer and Joao Pedro described as one of the most exciting attacking units in the league.

players.name: Mike Penders
players.note: Named as the young Belgian keeper Chelsea could turn to in place of Robert Sanchez.

players.name: Enzo Fernandez
players.note: Persistent rumours of a move to Manchester City; Chelsea want a replacement lined up before sanctioning an exit.

players.name: Liam Delap
players.note: Likely to join Nottingham Forest after being distanced from Chelsea's first-team training.

players.name: Mykhailo Mudryk
players.note: Possible loan interest from Strasbourg; a move to Leeds United is considered unlikely.

players.name: Alex Scott
players.note: Of interest to Chelsea as an Enzo Fernandez replacement, though Bournemouth are unwilling to sell.

players.name: Ethan Pinnock
players.note: The 33-year-old is set to join Coventry City for £5m plus £1m in add-ons, on a three-year deal with an option for a fourth.

players.name: Bernd Leno
players.note: Nutmegged by Cole Palmer for Chelsea's goal after being sold the dummy.

players.name: Josh King
players.note: Named in connection with Fulham's first goal, cited as an example of Robert Sanchez's poor positioning.

players.name: Ismaila Sarr

players.name: Jean-Philippe Mateta

players.name: Adam Wharton
players.note: Called a 'jewel' and close to irreplaceable for his sublime passing and tactical awareness, amid heavy transfer interest.

players.name: Ollie Watkins
players.note: Impending departure to Saudi Arabia, attributed to 'generational wealth', as part of a scattergun Villa rebuild.

players.name: Nicholas Jackson
players.note: Arriving at Villa, a significant shift in the club's striking options as Ollie Watkins leaves.

players.name: Emiliano Martinez
players.note: Named among the long-serving players whose high turnover is seen as a possible breaking point for Villa's European ambitions (surname only).

players.name: Ezri Konsa
players.note: Named among the long-serving players whose high turnover is seen as a possible breaking point for Villa's European ambitions (surname only).

players.name: Savio
players.note: Arrived at Spurs from Manchester City (previously Savinho) and impressed in the 5-1 Carabao Cup win over Charlton; part of a heavy bet on unproven ex-City talent.

players.name: Marmush
players.note: Named as arriving at Spurs from Manchester City; spelt 'Marmush' in the briefing, so the exact player is uncertain.

players.name: Niko Gonzalez
players.note: Signed by Newcastle from Manchester City for a reported £50m despite being seen as surplus at City; name form uncertain.

players.name: Mikey Moore
players.note: Impressed in Spurs' 5-1 Carabao Cup win over Charlton.

players.name: Robert Sanchez
players.note: Faces former club Brighton with Chelsea's title hopes seen as tethered to him; opponents may look to exploit the panic he transmits.
players.quote: I genuinely believe that Chelsea could challenge Arsenal for the title... but they have to change a goalkeeper.

players.name: Kieran Dewsbury-Hall
players.note: Standout performer in Everton's 4-0 Carabao Cup win over Preston.

players.name: Bruno Fernandes
players.note: Credited in the episode title for a brilliant display in the 5-2 win over Ipswich.

players.name: Harry Maguire
players.note: His handball in the buildup to a United goal was ruled accidental so the goal stood, which the panel argued rewarded a mis-hit shot.
players.quote: What [the rule] has effectively done is reward Harry Maguire for doing his job badly. By shooting off target he's rewarded, and that just shouldn't be how the rule is.

players.name: Kobbie Mainoo
players.note: Future subject to speculation despite strong performances.

players.name: Marcus Rashford
players.note: Future subject to speculation despite strong performances.

players.name: Harrison Armstrong
players.note: Attempted £40m sale of the academy prospect drew fan backlash, a case study in clubs selling homegrown 'pure profit' talent to satisfy PSR.

players.name: Micky van de Ven
players.note: Named among Spurs players lacking preseason integration as the side went two games without a point or a goal (surname only in the briefing).

players.name: Ryan Cherki
players.note: Scored his first brace, in the 4-1 win over Crystal Palace, providing a new creative spark for City.

players.name: Anthony Elanga
players.note: His goal in the 2-0 win at Tottenham was described as the crucial moment.

players.name: Morgan Gibbs-White
players.note: Liverpool's midfield struggled to contain him in a 2-2 draw in which Forest led twice.

players.name: Petrovic
players.note: Made heroic saves in the 1-1 draw with Everton (surname only in the briefing).

players.name: Emiliano Martinez
players.note: Called 'Emmy Martinez' in the briefing: his arrival at Chelsea is cited as evidence that a high-profile goalkeeping change can shift a title race, after the Robert Sanchez problem.

players.name: Nico Paz
players.note: Named as an example of the buy-back-and-sell schemes clubs use to manage their books.

players.name: Bukayo Saka
players.note: Scored the only goal at Villa Park, reacting quicker than Villa's defenders, in a win described as textbook title-winning efficiency.

players.name: Riccardo Calafiori
players.note: Named man of the match; his darting run created Arsenal's winner at Villa Park.

players.name: Eberechi Eze
players.note: Spelt 'Eza' in the briefing: provided the weighted pass for Arsenal's goal but was criticised for an instinct to drift infield and congest the structure.

players.name: Lucas Digne
players.note: Among nine Villa departures this summer, six of whom started the Europa League final.

players.name: Morgan Rogers
players.note: Listed among Villa's summer departures, part of a squad overhaul that has left them without a shot on target this season.

players.name: Gabriel Jesus
players.note: Written 'Gabrielle Jesus' in the briefing: linked to Barcelona for a fee around £15m.

players.name: Mykhailo Mudryk
players.note: Written 'Michaela Mudryk' in the briefing: linked to Tottenham and a reunion with Roberto De Zerbi, having been training in Battersea Park.

players.name: Jack Grealish
players.note: Potential loan to Everton following their loss of Danjuma.

players.name: Julian Alvarez
players.note: Wants to leave Spain and is rumoured to Arsenal, with Atletico seeking around £150m.

players.name: Arnaut Danjuma
players.note: Everton have lost him, prompting interest in a Jack Grealish loan (surname only in the briefing).

players.name: Bradley Barcola
players.note: Written 'Bradley Barker' in the briefing: linked to Liverpool, called a huge talent but not the best finisher.

players.name: Lionel Messi
players.note: Announced a second retirement from international football, saying he has nothing left to give and wants to make room for younger players.
players.quote: I have loved, and will always love being part of the national team. I've given it my all. I have nothing left to give.
